title: Shakira and Burna Boy Unite for 'Dai Dai', the Official FIFA World Cup 2026 Anthem
excerpt: The Colombian pop star and Nigerian Afrobeats icon join forces for the tournament's signature track as the World Cup heads to North America
body:
FIFA has unveiled 'Dai Dai' as the official anthem for the 2026 World Cup, a collaboration between Colombian superstar Shakira and Nigerian Afrobeats sensation Burna Boy. The track, which blends Latin rhythms with West African grooves, marks Shakira's return to the World Cup stage — a franchise she has effectively owned since 'Waka Waka' became the defining sound of the 2010 tournament in South Africa.

The pairing is commercially astute. Shakira commands a global audience of over 90 million Spotify listeners, while Burna Boy's Afrobeats-infused sound has crossed over from Lagos to London to Los Angeles. Together, they represent the increasingly global, genre-fluid direction of sports entertainment — a bet by FIFA that the tournament's cultural moment should sound as international as its participants.

For the Indian diaspora, the World Cup anthem signals the beginning of what promises to be the most accessible tournament in years. With matches spread across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, the 2026 edition is the first World Cup that NRIs in North America can attend without intercontinental travel. Early ticket data suggests strong interest from Indian-American and Indian-Canadian communities, particularly for matches in New York, Los Angeles, and Toronto.

The anthem also arrives amid broader World Cup preparations that have hit some turbulence. Hotel occupancy in US host cities has disappointed expectations, and infrastructure timelines remain tight. But the cultural machinery — halftime shows, anthems, and broadcast deals — is running at full speed. A previously announced halftime show featuring Madonna, Shakira, and BTS for the final underscores the scale of the entertainment investment.

'Dai Dai' is expected to drop on streaming platforms within the week, with a music video reportedly filmed across locations in Colombia, Nigeria, and New York City.
